title: Stoker plugins — plugin
description: `plugins/<key>/plugin.yaml` in a plugin registry: what a plugin is, across its versions. A registry is an index — this file and one file per version beside it, with the registry's `registry.yaml` at its root — and never a file host: each version names its files as release assets on the plugin's own repository, by URL and hash. Recipes name a plugin only by key and version. A Stoker host runs no version its administrator has not approved.

key.description: The folder's name, and the key every version's manifest declares. Reverse-DNS, and owned by namespace: a registry's `registry.yaml` says which publisher may publish under which prefix. Stoker's own plugins are `app.stokerhq.*`.

license.description: An SPDX licence expression — `MIT`, `LGPL-2.1-only`, `CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0` — or `LicenseRef-<name>` for one SPDX does not list. What a host may do with the files is the licence's answer, which is why a registry links to the author's own release rather than keeping a copy.

sourceCode.description: Where the plugin's source is kept. Each version also names the exact commit it was built from (`source`).

kind.description: Where the plugin's code runs, which is what decides how much trust it takes. `hook`: native code a bootstrap loads inside a game; assigned to a game, a release or a build (`plugins`). `mod`: files an install lays into a game for a mod loader — the loader itself (BepInEx), or a plugin for it; assigned like a hook. `integration`: a store SDK's replacement inside a game — bootstraps and their implementation — laid over the store's own file by the install plan. `server`: an extension stokerd loads at start, with stokerd's full rights; a host takes one only from a registry it trusts for that kind. `unpacker`: an assembly stokerd's ingest runs beside it, in a process of its own. `library`: a file other plugins load, never assigned and never run on its own. Every kind is valid in the format; what a registry accepts is its `policy` (`registry.yaml`).
